history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 127 / 'ISKCON Temple Patna' — this file was still written for seq 1359 with a unique id. The ISKCON Temple on Budh Marg, also called Sri Sri Radha Banke Bihari Ji Mandir or Golok Dham, is the largest temple in Patna and one of the biggest ISKCON temples — a 108-foot-tall, 84-pillared multi-storey complex on about 2–3 acres. The foundation stone was laid in 1984; the present temple opened to the public on 3 May 2022 and was reportedly built by Muslim artisans (cost estimated at Rs 51 crore, reportedly about Rs 100 crore on completion — verify). The presiding deities are Sri Sri Radha Banke Bihari Ji, Sri Sri Gaur Nitai and the Ram Darbar (Ram, Janaki, Lakshman, Hanuman), with additional altars of Jagannath, Baladev, Subhadra and Prabhupada. The complex includes a guesthouse, auditorium, restaurant and meditation centre, and runs daily Gita discourses and kirtans.

name: ISKCON Temple, Patna
town_description: Patna is the capital of Bihar, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world — ancient Pataliputra, seat of the Mauryan and Gupta empires. It stands on the southern bank of the Ganga and blends ancient heritage (Kumhrar, Agam Kuan) with modern institutions. The city is a major pilgrimage hub with Patna Sahib (Sikh), Patan Devi and Mahavir Mandir drawing devotees year-round.
